# Contributing to Entropy's Defiance

First off, thank you for considering contributing to Entropy's Defiance! It's people like you that make this app better for everyone.

## How Can I Contribute?

### Reporting Bugs

This section guides you through submitting a bug report. Following these guidelines helps maintainers understand your report, reproduce the behavior, and find related reports.

- Use the bug report template when creating an issue
- Be specific about the steps to reproduce the problem
- Include details about your environment (device, Android version, etc.)
- Include screenshots if they help explain the issue

### Suggesting Enhancements

This section guides you through submitting an enhancement suggestion, including completely new features and minor improvements to existing functionality.

- Use the feature request template when creating an issue
- Provide a clear and detailed explanation of the feature
- Explain why this enhancement would be useful
- Include any relevant mockups or examples

### Code Contributions

#### Setting Up Your Development Environment

1. Fork the repository
2. Clone your fork: `git clone https://github.com/yourusername/entropysdefiance.git`
3. Set up Android Studio with the project
4. Create a new branch for your feature: `git checkout -b feature/amazing-feature`

#### Making Changes

1. Make your changes in the new branch
2. Follow the coding style and conventions of the project
3. Write meaningful commit messages that explain your changes
4. Test your changes thoroughly

#### Submitting a Pull Request

1. Push your branch to your fork: `git push origin feature/amazing-feature`
2. Create a pull request from your branch to the main repository
3. Fill out the pull request template with details about your changes
4. Respond to any feedback during the review process

## Styleguides

### Git Commit Messages

- Use the present tense ("Add feature" not "Added feature")
- Use the imperative mood ("Move cursor to..." not "Moves cursor to...")
- Limit the first line to 72 characters or less
- Reference issues and pull requests liberally after the first line

### Kotlin Styleguide

- Follow the [Kotlin Coding Conventions](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/coding-conventions.html)
- Use descriptive variable names
- Add comments for complex logic
- Structure your code into small, focused functions

### UI Conventions

- Follow [Material Design guidelines](https://m3.material.io/)
- Maintain consistent UI patterns throughout the app
- Ensure all UI elements are accessible
- Support both light and dark themes

## Additional Notes

### Issue and Pull Request Labels

This section lists the labels we use to help us track and manage issues and pull requests.

- `bug`: Something isn't working
- `documentation`: Improvements or additions to documentation
- `enhancement`: New feature or request
- `good first issue`: Good for newcomers
- `help wanted`: Extra attention is needed

Thank you for contributing to Entropy's Defiance!
